idiom: bite off more than one can chew
meaning: to take on a task or responsibility that is too big to manage
example: He agreed to run the entire project alone, and soon realised he had bitten off more than he could chew.
origin: Probably from the image of taking a bite of food too large to chew; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a very large meal in one sitting
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes overcommitment, not eating

wrong_meanings.meaning: to chew gum noisily during a meeting
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom has nothing to do with chewing or manners

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to try anything new
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes accepting more than one can handle

explanation: 'Bite off more than one can chew' means to take on a task that is too large or difficult to complete successfully. It is common in both everyday and workplace speech.
